correctness.rationale: The gradient identity f_i=x_i²+s_1 x_i+s_2 has only one or two coordinate-value roots; parity and modulo-four binomial constraints establish exactly the indicator-point support for n≥5 and n≠2 (mod4). The explicit second-order Taylor form has smooth projective quadric even for 4|n, since its one-dimensional polar radical has Q=1. Odd n gives full-rank Jacobian and reduced points. For 4|n the gradient sum vanishes, the n−1 independent quadrics cut out a height-(n−1) regular sequence, giving total degree 2^{n−1}; exactly 2^{n−2} support points each have a one-dimensional Zariski tangent direction, hence every local length is exactly two. The standalone exact F4 enumeration for n=5,7,8,9 and quadratic checks corroborates but does not replace this infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The first-public initiating work arXiv:2610.00259v1 supplies general derivative-locus dimension formulas, extremal partition components, and coordinate-generic local rings, while expressly leaving smaller-dimensional components, primary decomposition and global reducedness open in its Section 7. The present result completes the full projective singular scheme of the third symmetric cubic in characteristic two for the stated dimensions, including non-coordinate indicator points, their exact local Artin rings, complete-intersection degree, and smooth quadratic tangent cones. Orzel 2509.05009v3 and the general symmetric-hypersurface literature do not state these conclusions. Exact result-index searches returned related but non-covering mathematical objects. Residual risk: older terminology or unpublished equivalent treatments cannot be excluded.

value.rationale: The geometric singular scheme of an elementary-symmetric cubic is a natural global invariant left unspecified by recently established dimension and coordinate-local results. The theorem provides a full infinite-family classification of locations, non-coordinate components, reducedness, local Artin length, and ordinary quadratic transverse type. The even case explains how every hypersurface ordinary quadratic point may have a doubled derivative scheme in characteristic two. This materially resolves a stated gap about smaller-dimensional components/global reducedness rather than merely extending a numerical table.
